ops.body:
Surfaced by the cc-context/bench v14 migration (P8): bench's `trajectory.py` initially kept one raw scrape because `parse_print_result` is strict — a malformed or truncated section in a `-p` (print-mode) stream fails the whole parse. The finishing lane then proved the leniency was empirically unreachable for bench: every raw file the consistency check examines strict-parses at record time (runner.run_one parses before record_from, and refresh_billed_usage runs strict over the same files earlier in write_report), so the scrape was removed and bench is fully typed as of cc-context main b7b2b77f. **No live consumer currently needs lenient parsing.**

The design item stands as a general upstream idea, demand-pending: a lenient mode on the print-parse entry point that yields typed messages for parseable elements and a typed `MalformedSection` marker (raw bytes + offset) for the rest, instead of raising. Strict stays the default — lenient would be opt-in for salvage/analytics consumers reading captures cc-transcript's own runner did not produce (crash-truncated streams, foreign harnesses). Owner module: the print-result parsing layer in cc-transcript core (Rust) with the Python view on top; per AGENTS.md § Ownership, no consumer-side regex fallbacks in the meantime. Build it when a real consumer with unparseable-in-practice captures shows up, not before.
